scope_notes: FY1 is the first course: no prior physics beyond comprehensive school. Motion stays at s = vt (and s = s0 + vt) and v = gt as linear models; forces, Newton's laws, energy and vectors are FY2/FY4.

Teacher's brief 2026-10-27 (Lauri): interactive scale simulations. fy1-1 has a 'Scale of the Universe' style zoom from the Planck length (about 1,6·10^-35 m) to the observable universe (diameter about 8,8·10^26 m), one power of ten at a time; fy1-2 has an 'If the Moon were only 1 pixel' style scrollable solar system to true scale, with Voyager 2 on it.

Voyager 2 data (teacher's brief 2026-10-27): distance, speed and one-way signal time computed from a chosen date with the uniform-motion model d = d0 + v(t - t0) from source data: heliopause crossing 2018-11-05 at 119,7 AU from the Sun (NASA/JPL), heliocentric speed 15,341 km/s (JPL Voyager mission status); 1 AU = 149 597 870,7 km, c = 299 792 458 m/s. Label the values as model values with their source (source: model); the model gives about 143 AU for February 2026, matching JPL's 143,05 AU. fy1-5 uses Voyager 2 as an example of s = s0 + vt.

Teacher's brief 2026-10-28 (Lauri): fy1-1 also gives a qualitative overview of the structure of matter (molecule, atom, nucleus and electrons, protons and neutrons, quarks; atom about 10^4–10^5 times its nucleus), of astronomical structures (Earth–Moon, Sun as a star, Solar System as one planetary system, heliosphere vs the reach of the Sun's gravity, Milky Way, galaxy groups and clusters, observable vs whole universe; nebulae, neutron stars and black holes as object types, not levels) and of the four fundamental interactions (gravitation, electromagnetic, strong, weak with beta decay) linked to one phenomenon each. No quantum mechanics, particle classification, stellar evolution or cosmology equations. The scale simulation stays the same zoom; it gained a water molecule, a neutron star and the event horizon of Sgr A*. fy1-2 links units and prefixes to these scales.

FY2.title: Fysiikka, ympäristö ja yhteiskunta
tavoitteet: perehtyy energiaan fysiikan keskeisenä käsitteenä
tuntee eri energialajeja ja energiantuotantotapoja

keskeiset_sisallot: energian tuotanto, teho, hyötysuhde ja energian siirtäminen
scope_notes: FY2 introduces energy forms without expressions; E_k, E_p, the work-energy theorem, vectors and cos α are FY4.

FY2 comes after FY1 and before FY3: students know SI units, prefixes and powers of ten, measurement and Delta x, graphs and the linear models s = vt and m = rho V (FY1 chapters, by name). Build on them; do not re-teach them.

No duplication with FY3 (taught later, it builds on FY2): FY2 has no work W = Fs or force, no Q = c m Delta T, no internal energy or first law, no heat-engine cycle or Carnot limit, no U-value or heat-conduction formulas, no radiative energy-balance model, and no product of chain efficiencies (fy3-15 does the chain and combined heat and power quantitatively). FY2 stays at energy forms, conservation, joule and kWh, P = E : t, one device's efficiency with an energy-flow (Sankey) picture, E = Hm, comparing production methods by orders of magnitude, transmission of electricity and heat qualitatively with simple loss percentages, and the environment.

Teacher's FY1-FY2 worksheet (FY01FY02_K2026.pdf, Lauri) sets the core vocabulary: energy forms mechanical (potential and kinetic), chemical (fuels, food, batteries), radiant, nuclear, electrical and thermal; energy is not created or destroyed but converts to less useful forms (E_alussa = E_lopussa for an isolated system); P = E/t with [P] = W and 1 kWh = 3,6 MJ; efficiency as the useful share of the energy taken in, by energy or by power; E = Hm; power plants as weather-dependent (wind, solar), well-adjustable (hydro, many fuel plants) and steady base load (nuclear); comparison criteria price, power, transportability, storability, safety and environmental impacts (emissions, climate change, land use, nature, waste, safety); greenhouse effect qualitatively (gases let solar radiation in but slow the outgoing heat radiation; humans add CO2 and methane).

Data in FY2 (Finnish energy statistics, emission factors, heating values) are real values with a named source (Tilastokeskus, Energiateollisuus, Fingrid, Motiva, IPCC) and year, rounded; mark invented situations as examples, never as statistics.

tavoitteet: osaa tutkia kokeellisesti voimaan ja liikkeeseen liittyviä ilmiöitä

keskeiset_sisallot: tasainen ja tasaisesti kiihtyvä suoraviivainen liike
kappaleiden vuorovaikutus ja voima sekä Newtonin lait
mekaanisen energian säilyminen ja mekaniikan energiaperiaate

scope_notes: FY4 continues FY1 (teacher 2026-10-29): build on FY1's measurement, graphs and the linear model (luku *Tasainen liike – nopeus, paikka ja kuvaajat*) without re-teaching them; FY4.1 (position, displacement, signed velocity) is the bridge and stays as it is.
Distinguish scalar and vector quantities where it matters (displacement, velocity, force), magnitudes plain and vectors with an overline in LaTeX (\overline{F}, teacher 2026-10-29).

Introduce acceleration from observations and graphs before the formula; develop Newton's laws one at a time, each from physical situations and, where possible, measured or simulated data, before equations.
Keep independent reasoning: complete model solutions, explain tasks with guided self-assessment, and a Sovella itsenäisesti task count that follows the module's goals.

Force diagrams are a core competency (teacher 2026-10-29, docs/force-diagrams.md): taught in full in Voimakuvio ja voimien yhteisvaikutus with the student guide "Voimakuvion piirtäminen", prepared in the chapters on Newton's laws and used again in every later chapter where forces act; each lesson's "fbd" lists the skills its tasks practise (identify, select, error, draw, equations; coverage.py checks), and every force chapter has a task where the student draws the diagram alone.

scope_notes: Plan approved by the teacher 2026-11-03 (17 chapters, order of his FY5 autumn 2026 timetable): gravitation in two chapters (law; circular orbits), harmonic force and spring potential energy together, then harmonic oscillation and the pendulum; reflection with diffraction, interference on its own; noise and hearing protection with acoustics in Ääni ympäristössämme; ultrasound imaging in the applied chapter.

FY5 builds on FY4 (Newton's laws, force diagrams, energy) without re-teaching it: every chapter where forces act uses the force-diagram skills of docs/force-diagrams.md; vectors with an overline (\overline{F}); velocity, acceleration and force always in different colours (force red, velocity blue, acceleration orange as in FY4).

No angular quantities (ω, rad/s) for circular motion and no rotational dynamics (LOPS täsmennys); circular motion uses period, rotation frequency and v = 2πr/T. Gravitational constant written γ as in Finnish textbooks (G in English).

Old FY05 simulations in the site root fy05/ (momentti, tasapaino, tukki, ratanopeus, ympyraliike, nyppyla, kiertorata, painottomuus, varahtely, harmoninen-varahtely, vaimeneva-varahtely, aalto-langassa, interferenssi, seisova-aalto, doppler) are starting points for ideas only; new sims follow the house rules (LaTeX labels, speed control, assets/sims/fy5/).

tavoitteet: osaa tutkia kokeellisesti sähköön liittyviä ilmiöitä ja tehdä sähköopin perusmittauksia

scope_notes: Plan approved by the teacher 2026-11-03 (16 chapters from the LOPS FY6 contents, not from a timetable): circuit and measuring first, then Ohm, connections, Kirchhoff with potential, power and household energy, source voltage and batteries; then charge with Coulomb's law, the uniform field, potential, the capacitor; semiconductors with the solar cell, electrical safety, an applied electric-car chapter.
Capacitor charging and discharging only qualitatively (no exponential function); no capacitor connections (LOPS täsmennys). Semiconductors as circuit components, not materials physics.

FY6 builds on FY2 (energy, power, kWh) and FY4 (force, energy) without re-teaching them; vectors with an overline (\overline{E}, \overline{F}); force and field arrows in different colours, velocity, acceleration and force always in different colours (force red, velocity blue, acceleration orange as in FY4). Conventional current direction from + to −; electron flow named separately where it matters.
Circuit diagrams use the IEC symbols of Finnish textbooks (resistor a rectangle); every label in them LaTeX. Division written with a colon in prose (U : I), \frac in display formulas.

scope_notes: Plan approved by the teacher 2026-11-03 (16 chapters from LOPS 2021 and the MAOL täsmennykset only; no commercial textbook or timetable structure). The climate-change link is an optional box in chapter 2 (absorption bands), not its own chapter; the de Broglie wavelength is not taught at all (teacher 2026-11-03).

Photon energy E = hf, h = 6,626·10^-34 Js; electronvolt allowed with conversion shown by substitution. Hydrogen levels E_n = -13,6 eV / n^2 given as data, not derived. No Schrödinger equation; the wave-mechanical model is qualitative (standing waves, probability, orbital as a threshold region).

Decay law N = N0 (1/2)^(t/T½) and N = N0 e^(-λt) with A = λN; exponential fitting done with Graphical Analysis-style data (TVT). Binding energy and reaction energy from atomic masses in u with c^2; 1 u = 931,5 MeV/c^2.

Doses: absorbed dose Gy, effective dose Sv; Finnish figures from STUK with source and year. Old FY08_*.html simulations in the site root (valosahkoinen, spektri, bohr, kaksoisrako, tunneloituminen, alfahajoaminen, beetahajoaminen, fissio, fuusio, geiger, lapaisykyky) are starting points for ideas only; new sims follow the house rules (LaTeX labels, speed control, assets/sims/fy8/).
